summary.en: Colleagues in Spain quickly switch to informal tú, while guests and older strangers receive polite usted.

body.en:
From season 1, episode 1.

In the kitchen, Rocio greets the new receptionist with *tú eres* ... *¿verdad?* and tells her *¡Conmigo siempre! Deja el usted para los clientes.* Upstairs, Carmen addresses Clara with formal *usted* forms too: *¡Mire dentro de esta maleta!* Peninsula Spanish draws a clear, friendly line between everyday *tú* and respectful *usted*.

Peers, friends, coworkers, and family members in Spain almost immediately *tutear*—using *tú* verb endings (*eres*, *tienes*, *mira*, *deja*). With hotel guests, older strangers, or someone you have not met yet, switch to *usted*, which pairs with third-person singular verb forms (*es*, *tiene*, *mire*, *disculpe*) and possessive *su*.

In the plural, speakers in Spain distinguish informal *vosotros* among colleagues and friends (*mirad la nevera*) from formal *ustedes* when addressing guests (*ustedes me están salvando*).
